subtopic_detail: Cyclical irritability confined to the ten days before menses with a symptom free follicular phase
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 29 year old primary school teacher who describes two years of irritability, tearfulness, breast tenderness and bloating that begin about ten days before each period and settle within two days of the bleeding starting.

She has received two formal complaints at work about how she spoke to colleagues, both in the week before a period, and she is frightened of losing her job. A prospective daily symptom record kept over three cycles shows a rating of zero on most days between the end of bleeding and mid cycle, with scores rising steeply from day eighteen. She has migraine with visual aura about twice a month. She uses condoms for contraception and has no intrauterine device in place. She has no thoughts of self harm.

data_table.Examination: Euthymic and pleasant at this mid follicular visit, affect full range, no psychomotor change, body mass index 24 kg/m2
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone 1.7 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), haemoglobin 128 g/L (115-155), ferritin 42 micrograms/L (30-300)

lead_in: What is the most appropriate first line pharmacological treatment?

options.text: Sertraline 50 mg taken from day fourteen of the cycle until menstruation starts
options.rationale: Serotonergic antidepressants are the most effective treatment for severe cyclical premenstrual symptoms, and unlike their use in depression the benefit appears within a day or two, which is what makes dosing restricted to the luteal phase as effective as continuous dosing while halving total exposure. The prospectively confirmed symptom free follicular phase is what establishes the diagnosis and justifies intermittent dosing. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders

options.text: A combined oral contraceptive containing drospirenone taken continuously
options.rationale: Continuous combined hormonal contraception is a legitimate option for this condition and drospirenone containing formulations have the best evidence, but migraine with aura is an absolute contraindication to any combined preparation because of the stroke risk. The distinction from the correct answer is entirely her headache history rather than the efficacy of the drug. (Source: Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare medical eligibility criteria)
source_refs: Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare medical eligibility criteria

options.text: Micronised progesterone 200 mg nightly during the second half of the cycle
options.rationale: Luteal phase progesterone and progestogens have been tested repeatedly in this condition and do not outperform placebo, and in some women progestogens reproduce the symptoms. The persistence of this prescribing rests on the mistaken idea that the disorder reflects progesterone deficiency. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders

options.text: A gonadotrophin releasing hormone agonist with oestrogen and progestogen add back
options.rationale: Medical ovarian suppression is highly effective and is used as a diagnostic and therapeutic step, but it is third line because of bone density loss and vasomotor effects, and add back therapy is required. Starting here skips two safer tiers of treatment. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders

options.text: Evening primrose oil 1000 mg twice daily through the second half of the cycle
options.rationale: Trials of evening primrose oil show benefit for cyclical breast tenderness only, with no effect on the mood and irritability symptoms that are causing her occupational problem. Offering it as the treatment for a disorder threatening her employment understates the severity. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is distinguished from ordinary premenstrual symptoms by severity and functional impairment, and from a mood disorder with premenstrual worsening by the presence of a genuinely symptom free interval after menstruation. That distinction cannot be made retrospectively, which is why two cycles of prospective daily ratings are required before treatment is committed to. The underlying mechanism appears to be abnormal central sensitivity to normal luteal phase changes in progesterone metabolites rather than any abnormality of circulating hormone concentrations, which explains why measuring hormones is unhelpful and why supplementing progesterone fails. Treatment options in order are serotonergic antidepressants continuously or in the luteal phase, continuous combined hormonal contraception, and ovarian suppression, with cognitive behavioural therapy effective in parallel. Bilateral oophorectomy with hysterectomy is definitive but is reserved for women who have responded to a trial of ovarian suppression and have completed their family.
key_points: A prospectively documented symptom free follicular phase is required for the diagnosis
Serotonergic antidepressants work within days here, allowing luteal phase only dosing
Circulating hormone concentrations are normal and do not need measuring
Luteal phase progesterone does not outperform placebo
Migraine with aura rules out any combined hormonal contraceptive option
explanation.pearls: The rapid onset of benefit is the diagnostic giveaway as well as the dosing rationale: if a woman with cyclical symptoms reports that a serotonergic antidepressant helped within forty eight hours rather than over the two to four weeks expected in depression, that response pattern supports the premenstrual diagnosis rather than an underlying depressive episode.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists: Premenstrual disorders

subtopic_detail: Agitation with racing thoughts and three hours of sleep three weeks after starting an antidepressant
stem:
You are the general practitioner reviewing a 27 year old graphic designer three weeks after starting escitalopram 10 mg daily for a depressive episode. Before treatment she had six weeks of low mood, loss of interest, sleeping eleven hours a night, a 5 kg weight gain and a leaden heaviness in her limbs.

She now sleeps three hours a night and describes herself as revved up and miserable at the same time. Her thoughts race, she is irritable with her partner, she cries daily, and she has begun four separate work projects between two and four in the morning. She says her mood is still as low as it was and that new thoughts of hurting herself have started this week, which frighten her. She denies feeling elated or confident and denies any sense that she needs less sleep. At twenty two she had a fortnight of sleeping little and painting through the night after returning from a trip, which her sister called manic at the time; she never saw anyone about it. Her mother takes lithium.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 96 beats per minute, blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius
data_table.Examination: Restless in the chair, pressured and rapid speech with a dysphoric affect, no grandiose content, no hallucinations, fully oriented
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone 1.5 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), urine drug screen negative, full blood count and electrolytes within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Increase the escitalopram to 20 mg daily and review her in two weeks
options.rationale: Dose escalation is the standard response to partial improvement at three weeks, and it is the trap here: the activation, reduced sleep and racing thoughts have appeared since the drug was started, so increasing it intensifies the very state causing the risk. Escalation would be right if she were simply not yet responding, with unchanged sleep and no activation. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline

options.text: Add diazepam 5 mg twice daily and review her sleep and her agitation in one week
options.rationale: A benzodiazepine is a reasonable short term adjunct for agitation and insomnia in this state, but adding it while leaving the antidepressant running treats the symptom and not the driver, and sedation can mask the deterioration you need to be able to see. It has a role alongside the correct answer, not instead of it. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

options.text: Add zolpidem at night for sleep and review her agitation in one week
options.rationale: Treating the three hours of sleep as primary insomnia misreads a mood state in which the sleep change is a symptom rather than the problem, and zolpidem in particular can produce disinhibition and complex sleep behaviours in agitated patients. The sleep will correct when the underlying state does. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

options.text: Stop the escitalopram and start quetiapine, with psychiatric review this week
options.rationale: Depressed mood occurring together with pressured speech, racing thoughts, psychomotor activation and markedly reduced sleep is a mixed state, and the previous fortnight of reduced sleep with increased activity plus the family history of lithium use place her on the bipolar spectrum. Antidepressant monotherapy is withdrawn and an agent effective in bipolar depression substituted, urgently, because mixed states carry the highest suicide risk of any mood presentation. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline

options.text: Switch to mirtazapine at night and review her sleep and mood in two weeks
options.rationale: Switching between antidepressant classes is the right move for a non-responder with insomnia, but any antidepressant given without a mood stabilising agent can sustain or worsen a mixed state, so changing the molecule does not change the mechanism of harm. A two week review is also too long for someone with new self harm thoughts. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline

explanation.summary: Mixed features are depressive and manic symptoms occurring at the same time, and they are missed constantly because clinicians look for elevated mood and find none, while the patient reports feeling worse and is assumed to need more antidepressant. The features to hunt for are psychomotor agitation, racing or crowded thoughts, pressured speech, irritability and a reduction in sleep in someone who still describes their mood as low. Atypical depressive features such as hypersomnia, increased appetite, weight gain and leaden paralysis, an early age of onset, a family history of bipolar disorder and a past episode of reduced sleep with increased activity all raise the prior probability of bipolarity before any drug is given. Antidepressant monotherapy in this setting can precipitate or prolong the mixed state, and mixed states carry a higher suicide rate than either pure pole, which is why the response is urgent rather than watchful. Management is withdrawal of the antidepressant with introduction of a mood stabilising agent, short term sedation if needed, and specialist involvement within days.
key_points: Low mood with agitation, racing thoughts and reduced sleep defines a mixed state
Absence of elevated mood does not exclude it and is the usual reason it is missed
Hypersomnia, weight gain and leaden paralysis flag possible bipolarity before treatment
Antidepressant monotherapy can precipitate or sustain the mixed state
Mixed states carry the highest suicide risk of any mood presentation
explanation.pearls: Ask every patient with depression about a past period of several days with reduced need for sleep and increased goal directed activity before writing the first antidepressant script, because a positive answer plus a first degree relative with bipolar disorder shifts the treatment from an antidepressant to a mood stabilising agent and is the single cheapest way to avoid this presentation.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists: Mood disorders clinical practice guideline

subtopic_detail: Punching and shouting in the second half of the night in a veteran assumed to have trauma nightmares
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 64 year old former soldier whose wife has asked for the appointment. For eighteen months he has shouted, kicked and punched in his sleep, and last month he struck her forearm hard enough to bruise it and fell out of bed himself.

The episodes happen in the early hours rather than soon after he goes to bed. When she wakes him he is immediately lucid and can describe a dream of fighting off a man breaking into a shed; none of the dreams involve his service. His post-traumatic stress disorder was treated with trauma focused therapy ten years ago and he has had no flashbacks, avoidance or hypervigilance since. He mentions in passing that he has been constipated for two years and that his wife now does the cooking because he cannot smell whether food has turned.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 64 beats per minute, blood pressure 138/82 mmHg with no postural drop, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, SpO2 97 percent on room air, temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius
data_table.Examination: Mild reduction in right arm swing on walking, no resting tremor, tone normal, Montreal Cognitive Assessment 27 out of 30, post-traumatic stress checklist score in the non-clinical range
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone 2.1 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), vitamin B12 410 pmol/L (150-700), full blood count and electrolytes within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Start prazosin at night and review the frequency of the episodes in four weeks
options.rationale: Prazosin reduces trauma related nightmares in post-traumatic stress disorder, and that is the diagnosis being assumed here, but his checklist is in the non-clinical range and the dream content has nothing to do with his service. Treating the wrong condition also delays recognition of what the episodes actually predict. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

options.text: Refer for polysomnography and make the sleep environment safe in the meantime
options.rationale: Dream enactment in the second half of the night with immediate full alertness on waking and accurate dream recall is the pattern of rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder, and the diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating loss of the normal muscle atonia during that sleep stage. Immediate safety measures matter because injury to the bed partner is the presenting harm. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association: Parasomnias)

options.text: Restart trauma focused psychological therapy and review the episodes in four weeks
options.rationale: Recurrence of post-traumatic stress disorder would bring daytime re-experiencing, avoidance and hyperarousal alongside the nightmares, and he has none of these. The dream content that he recalls is also unrelated to his deployments, which is the specific feature separating this from a trauma nightmare. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

options.text: Start quetiapine at night and review the frequency of the episodes in four weeks
options.rationale: Sedating him does not restore muscle atonia, and dopamine blocking agents are specifically hazardous in this group because many of these patients are in the prodrome of a synuclein disease and can develop severe sensitivity to antipsychotics. This is the option most likely to cause harm. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association: Parasomnias)

options.text: Arrange an electroencephalogram and review the episodes with the result in four weeks
options.rationale: Nocturnal frontal lobe seizures are the differential worth naming, and they produce brief stereotyped hyperkinetic episodes clustering many times a night with postictal confusion rather than a single coherent enacted dream with instant lucidity. A routine interictal recording would also be normal in both conditions. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association: Parasomnias)

explanation.summary: Rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder is the loss of the normal paralysis of that sleep stage, so the patient physically acts out dream content, typically defensive or violent, in the second half of the night when that sleep predominates. It is separated from non-rapid eye movement parasomnias such as sleep terrors by the timing, by immediate full orientation on waking and by detailed dream recall, and from trauma nightmares by dream content unrelated to the trauma and by the absence of daytime post-traumatic symptoms. Its importance is prognostic: the great majority of people with the idiopathic form eventually develop Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or multiple system atrophy, often more than a decade later, and subtle constipation, loss of smell and reduced arm swing are the early markers of that process. Management begins with making the bedroom safe, removing bedside furniture, padding the floor and considering separate beds, and melatonin is generally preferred to clonazepam as first line drug treatment in older people because of falls and sedation. How much of the prognosis to disclose is a genuine ethical question that is best negotiated with the patient rather than dumped or withheld.
key_points: Second half of the night, instant lucidity and matching dream recall define the disorder
Polysomnography confirms it by showing absent muscle atonia in rapid eye movement sleep
Constipation, loss of smell and reduced arm swing mark an evolving synuclein disease
Bedroom safety measures come before any drug treatment
Dopamine blocking drugs risk severe sensitivity reactions in this group
explanation.pearls: Melatonin at doses of 2 to 10 mg at night is preferred over clonazepam 0.5 mg in this population, because clonazepam worsens the falls, daytime sedation and obstructive sleep apnoea that older patients already carry, while the injury risk being treated is to the bed partner as much as to the patient.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

subtopic_detail: New online gambling debt and uncharacteristic sexual behaviour in a man treated for restless legs
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 58 year old plumber who attends with his wife. She has discovered sixty thousand dollars of debt accumulated through online sports betting over the past eight months, on accounts he opened without telling her.

He has never gambled before, not even on a work sweepstake, and he is tearful and ashamed in the room. She adds that he has been shopping compulsively online and that his sexual demands have changed in a way she finds distressing. He says he has tried to stop several times and cannot. He denies feeling elated or unusually confident, says he sleeps his usual seven hours and needs them, and has taken no new substances. His pramipexole for restless legs was increased six months ago because the symptoms had spread to his arms, and he also takes atorvastatin.

data_table.Examination: Dysphoric and tearful, normal rate of speech, no flight of ideas, no grandiosity, no psychotic features, Montreal Cognitive Assessment 29 out of 30
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone 1.8 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), ferritin 58 micrograms/L (30-300), liver function and electrolytes within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Refer him to a gambling counselling service and continue his current treatment
options.rationale: Counselling is part of the answer but leaving the drug unchanged leaves the cause in place, and psychological treatment alone performs poorly while dopaminergic stimulation continues. This would be correct if the behaviour predated the prescription. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology)

options.text: Start naltrexone daily and refer him to a gambling counselling service
options.rationale: Opioid antagonists have modest evidence in primary gambling disorder and are worth considering there, but adding a second drug to manage the adverse effect of a first one, while that first drug continues, is the wrong order of operations. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

options.text: Start sodium valproate and refer him to a gambling counselling service
options.rationale: A mood stabiliser presumes a manic or hypomanic episode, and he has normal sleep, no elevated mood, no grandiosity and preserved insight with genuine distress about the behaviour, none of which fits mania. The behaviour is also confined to reward seeking rather than being part of a global change in drive. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Stop the pramipexole abruptly tonight and refer him to a gambling counselling service
options.rationale: Ceasing the drug is right but doing it abruptly risks dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome, an unpleasant and sometimes prolonged state of anxiety, panic, pain, sweating and drug craving that does not respond to other dopaminergic agents. The difference from the correct answer is the rate, not the direction. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology)

options.text: Withdraw the pramipexole slowly and refer him to a gambling counselling service
options.rationale: New onset gambling, compulsive shopping and hypersexuality beginning after a dose increase of a dopamine agonist is a recognised and dose related adverse effect mediated by stimulation of mesolimbic receptors, and the behaviour usually resolves when the drug is withdrawn. A gradual reduction avoids the withdrawal syndrome, and the restless legs are then reassessed with iron studies and an alternative agent. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology)

explanation.summary: Impulse control disorders complicate dopamine agonist treatment in a substantial minority of patients, with reported rates of around one in six in Parkinson disease and appreciable rates when the same drugs are used at lower doses for restless legs syndrome. The four classic behaviours are pathological gambling, compulsive shopping, hypersexuality and binge eating, and they are dose related, more common in younger men with a personal or family history of substance use, and driven by stimulation of receptors in the mesolimbic reward pathway. Patients almost never volunteer them, both from shame and because they do not connect the behaviour to a tablet prescribed for their legs, so the question has to be asked directly and repeatedly, and the warning has to be given to the patient and to a partner when the drug is started. The behaviour usually remits on withdrawal but the withdrawal itself must be gradual because abrupt cessation causes a distinct agonist withdrawal syndrome. In restless legs specifically, dopamine agonists also cause augmentation, in which symptoms start earlier in the day and spread to the arms, which is why alpha 2 delta ligands such as gabapentin have displaced them as first line treatment.
key_points: Gambling, shopping, hypersexuality and binge eating are the four classic behaviours
The effect is dose related and occurs at restless legs doses, not only Parkinson doses
Patients rarely volunteer it, so it must be asked about directly at each review
Withdrawal must be gradual to avoid dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome
Behaviour usually remits once the agonist is withdrawn
explanation.pearls: Symptoms of restless legs that start earlier in the day and spread from the legs to the arms, as his did before the dose was increased, are augmentation rather than disease progression, and increasing the agonist in response is the error that both worsens augmentation and raises the impulse control risk; the correct response is to check ferritin, aiming above 75 micrograms/L, and to move to an alpha 2 delta ligand.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

subtopic_detail: Silence at school with loud fluent speech at home in a six year old in her second year of schooling
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 6 year old girl whose teacher has told her parents she may need an autism assessment. In fourteen months at school she has never spoken a word to a teacher or to another child, communicating by nodding, pointing and writing.

At home she talks constantly, argues with her older brother, invents elaborate games with her cousins and does impressions of her teacher that make the family laugh. Her mother reports that she chats in the car right up to the school gate and then stops. In the consulting room she sits close to her mother, makes eye contact with you, smiles at a joke, and freezes and looks at the floor when you ask her a direct question. She reached all her language milestones on time and has no repetitive behaviours, no restricted interests and no sensory aversions. Her father describes himself as having been painfully shy as a boy.

data_table.Examination: Reciprocal eye contact and shared smiling with her mother and with the examiner, imaginative play observed with the toys, freezing and averted gaze on direct questioning, no dysmorphic features
data_table.Investigations: Audiology assessment normal bilaterally, speech pathology screen of receptive language age appropriate, full blood count within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Refer for a formal autism spectrum assessment and review her after the report
options.rationale: This is the referral the school has asked for and it is the wrong one: autism requires persistent deficits in social communication across contexts, and she shows reciprocal eye contact, shared enjoyment, imaginative play and fluent conversational speech at home and in the room. The situational nature of the silence is what separates the two. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Refer for a speech pathology assessment of expressive language delay
options.rationale: An expressive language disorder would affect speech in every setting including the home, and her speech there is fluent, complex and age appropriate, with normal milestones and a normal receptive screen. Speech pathology may still join the school programme, but not to assess a delay that is not present. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne clinical practice guideline)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne clinical practice guideline

options.text: Refer for a behavioural programme using graded speaking exposure at school
options.rationale: Consistent failure to speak in specific social situations where speaking is expected, despite speaking normally elsewhere, for more than a month beyond the first year of school, is an anxiety disorder, and the treatment is a graded behavioural programme run with the school that moves from non-verbal responses through whispering to single words with one adult and then widens the circle. Starting behavioural treatment early matters because the silence becomes self reinforcing across school years. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Start fluoxetine and review her speaking at school in eight weeks
options.rationale: A serotonin reuptake inhibitor has evidence in this condition but is reserved for children who do not respond to an adequate behavioural programme or whose impairment is severe, because the behavioural approach works in most children without drug exposure at this age. Starting here reverses the order. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

options.text: Advise the school to avoid asking her direct questions for a term
options.rationale: Removing the pressure to speak feels kind and is a reasonable first step within a structured programme, but as the whole plan it is avoidance, and accommodation without graded exposure predicts persistence into later school years. The distinction from the correct answer is that exposure is reduced temporarily in order to be rebuilt, not abandoned. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Selective mutism is classified with the anxiety disorders and affects roughly one child in one hundred and forty, with onset typically before the age of five and a delay to diagnosis often measured in years. It is regularly misread as autism, as shyness, as oppositional behaviour or as a language disorder, and the discriminating question is always whether the child speaks normally in any setting: fluent conversational speech at home with reciprocal social engagement excludes both autism and an expressive language disorder. Comorbid social anxiety disorder is present in most cases and a family history of anxiety is common. Treatment is behavioural, using stimulus fading and graded exposure delivered in the school with the teacher as a co-therapist, and typically progresses from non-verbal responses to whispered single words with one trusted adult before widening to peers and the classroom. Serotonin reuptake inhibitors are added for children who do not respond or whose impairment is severe, and outcomes are substantially better when treatment begins in the first years of school.
key_points: Speech is normal in at least one setting, which rules out a language disorder
Reciprocal social engagement and imaginative play argue strongly against autism
Duration must exceed one month and must not be limited to the first month of school
Graded exposure with the school is first line and works in most young children
Serotonin reuptake inhibitors are reserved for non-response or severe impairment
explanation.pearls: The most useful single question to a parent is whether the child speaks freely to anyone at all, because a child who converses fluently at home has by definition preserved language and social reciprocity, and the answer redirects the referral from a twelve month autism assessment waiting list to a behavioural programme that can start next week.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne clinical practice guideline
